ui_strings.ai_content_1:
Steps:
1. Click the text box and enter a description (e.g., a cat)
2. Click the generate button next to the description and wait for AI generation
3. Image generation complete

Tip:
 You can use your native language, but English descriptions are recommended for more accurate results
ui_strings.ai_content_2:
Steps:
1. Click the camera icon, select a photo or take a new one, crop and upload (e.g., a selfie of a little boy)
2. Click the generate button and wait for AI generation
3. Image generation complete

Tip:
 With smart inference enabled, no prompt words needed
ui_strings.ai_content_3:
Steps:
1. Upload a photo
2. Enter modification prompts (e.g., a little girl in a princess dress)
3. Go to advanced settings - uncheck "Smart Inference"
4. Click generate button, AI will generate based on your photo and prompts

Tip:
 Disable smart inference to reconstruct image content using your own prompt descriptions

ui_strings.my_clock_play_plan_home_tip:
Weekly repeat plan: Set recurring face display rules by weekday and time range. You can choose specific days of the week to repeat, for example display a selected face from 9:00-18:00 Monday through Friday. If no repeat days are set, the plan runs only once and turns off automatically when finished.

Specific date plan: Set face display plans by specific dates and time ranges. Ideal for one-time occasions such as birthdays, holidays, and anniversaries. For example, show a birthday-themed face only on a certain birthday. The plan turns off automatically when finished.

ui_strings.tomato_tips_context: The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method that uses a timer set to 25 minutes to help improve work efficiency and focus. In practice, users choose a task, start a 25-minute timer, and work diligently. After the timer ends, take a 5-minute break. After completing four cycles, take a 15-30 minute break. This method can significantly improve concentration, prevent fatigue, help users perceive time more accurately, and provide a strong sense of accomplishment.

ui_strings.wifi_24g_hint_1: Devices can only be connected to the 2.4 GHz band on Wi-Fi routers.
ui_strings.wifi_24g_hint_10: Example of one Wi-Fi network: As seen in the iPhone Wi-Fi settings below, this is an example of only one Wi-Fi network name that belongs to the user, MyHome-WiFi.
ui_strings.wifi_24g_hint_11: I have more than one network name that belongs to me. How do I identify my 2.4 GHz band network?
ui_strings.wifi_24g_hint_12: From your smartphone's Wireless settings page, look at the names of your Wi-Fi networks.
ui_strings.wifi_24g_hint_13: A 2.4 GHz network may have 24G, 2.4, or 24 appended to the end of the network name. For example: MyHome-WiFi2.4
ui_strings.wifi_24g_hint_14: A 5 GHz network may have 5G or 5 appended to the end of the network name, for example MyHome-WiFi5
ui_strings.wifi_24g_hint_15: Example of two Wi-Fi network names: Here is an example where the user has more than one network name that belongs to him. He needs to make sure that he is connected to the 2.4 GHz band to set up his device:
ui_strings.wifi_24g_hint_2: All Wi-Fi routers have a 2.4 GHz band.
ui_strings.wifi_24g_hint_3: Newer routers are often dual-band router, with 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands.
ui_strings.wifi_24g_hint_4: If both of your 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz Wi-Fi bands have the same name and password, you will not have any problem connecting your Smart Home device regardless of which Wi-Fi network band your smartphone is connected to. You do not need to read further.
ui_strings.wifi_24g_hint_5: Easy check of your smartphone's Wi-Fi connection
ui_strings.wifi_24g_hint_6: To find out whether you need to connect to a different Wi-Fi network to set up your device, go to Settings > WLAN on your smartphone.
ui_strings.wifi_24g_hint_7: How many Wi-Fi networks do you see that belong to you?
ui_strings.wifi_24g_hint_8: I see one network: If you only see one Wi-Fi network name that belongs to you, you can proceed with setting up your device with this Wi-Fi connection. (see IMAGE 1 below).
ui_strings.wifi_24g_hint_9: I see two or more networks: If you see two or more Wi-Fi network names that belong to you, then one may be a 5 GHz band. Please continue reading the article below Image 1.
